transcript.text: micrwave keeps tripping the eletric, not every time but like 1 in 3 when i press start, whole kitchen goes off. had to reset the fuse box 4 times today

⚠ Stop using this appliance
Please don't keep resetting the trip. Leave the appliance unplugged and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer before using it again. Because your microwave is tripping the main kitchen fuse when you press start, this is a serious electrical fault inside the appliance—most likely a short in the magnetron or high-voltage capacitor. You must stop using it immediately and do not keep resetting the fuse box; forcing power through a short circuit can cause fire damage to your wiring. Please arrange for an engineer to inspect it before use again.

reading.symptom: keeps tripping the electric when pressing start

plan: Safety: a supply trip hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
The fault they reported is: "keeps tripping the electric when pressing start". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.
They asked about something unsafe (repeated reset): do not explain how to do it; the fixed safety wording is shown separately. Offer the safe alternative.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.
